concerns.text: FR-001 requires the system to *retrieve* the three open datasets and parse them into a unified DataFrame. T001 only *verifies* that required columns exist; it does not perform the required retrieval or parsing, and the plan notes that none of the listed sources actually contain all required variables, so the task cannot satisfy FR-001.

FR-001 also mandates downloading the datasets. T002 assumes the datasets are already verified and available, but given the earlier finding that the sources lack required variables, this task cannot fulfill the functional requirement and thus weakens the specification.
FR-008/FR-009 require a unit‑metadata file named `adhesion_units.json`. T003 creates `adhesion_raw_units.json`, breaking the contract and preventing downstream validation of unit consistency.

SC-001 states that the model must achieve R² ≥ 0.5. T010 allows the pipeline to continue with a `null_result` when no model meets the CI ≥ 0.5 threshold, thereby permitting the project to pass without satisfying the success criterion – a direct weakening of SC-001.

SC-002 requires a permutation‑test p‑value < 0.05 for significance. T012 only checks that the file exists and that the CI asserts the value is < 0.05 for a “significant” finding; it does not enforce a failure when the p‑value ≥ 0.05, allowing the pipeline to succeed without meeting SC-002.

SC-004 demands SHAP‑value stability with a standard deviation < 0.1. T015 permits a `null` result with an explanatory note when fewer than three folds yield SHAP values, effectively allowing the stability requirement to be bypassed.

The constitution (Principle I – Reproducibility) requires that random seeds be pinned in all code. No task mentions setting or recording random seeds, violating the non‑negotiable reproducibility principle.

T004 runs a smoke‑test on a synthetic subset but does not verify that the full preprocessing steps (median imputation, one‑hot encoding, unit conversion) have been correctly applied, leaving FR-002 and FR-008/009 effectively untested.
